subject: Medford Square Mixed-Use Rezoning
overview: The Planning and Permitting Committee and Community Development Board held a community meeting to present a draft rezoning proposal for Medford Square that enables mixed-use development through a height-incentive system. Residents and city officials discussed the project's impact on traffic, parking capacity, and neighborhood character ahead of a formal public hearing scheduled for March 25th.

items.title: Introduction to the Rezoning Process
items.summary: Councilor Matt Leming explained the collaborative procedure between the City Council and the Community Development Board to update zoning for a more vibrant Medford Square.

items.title: Medford Square Mixed-Use Proposal
items.summary: Consultant Emily Innes detailed the transition from use-separated zoning to four new mixed-use districts that allow building heights to increase from base levels in exchange for community benefits like affordable housing.

items.title: Dimensional and Environmental Standards
items.summary: Presenters introduced development standards including building frontage requirements, 'green scores' for ecological health, and a proposed 'daylight score' to protect solar access for residential neighbors.

items.title: Feedback on Traffic and Infrastructure
items.summary: Residents expressed concerns regarding the ownership of the National Grid substation and argued that existing congestion from the Interstate 93 rotary necessitates higher parking ratios for new developments.

items.title: Feedback on Building Height and Green Space
items.summary: Community members highlighted the potential for mid-rise buildings to shadow residential homes and requested more substantial green space requirements and better pedestrian connectivity to the Mystic River.
